# 193 — PR explainer (HIGH tier, full lane + quiz)

> **Tier note, stated up front rather than buried.** The spec guessed LOW and the verifier
> independently agreed — but the verifier's stated basis was *"diff is 18 tracked lines"*, which
> counted only the two MODIFIED files and omitted the new 201-line `test_audit_number_boundary.js`.
> Measured properly (`git diff --cached --numstat`), code + tests = **219 lines**, over the LOW
> lane's 150-line cap. Item 190's attempt 1 failed on exactly this arithmetic; applying its
> precedent, the operator re-tiered this **HIGH** before merging and wrote the full explainer and
> 5-question quiz below. Nothing was deleted to fit a number. No NEVER-list surface is engaged, so
> autonomy (c) still permits the merge — the tier changes the *paperwork*, not the outcome.

## Goal

Stop the rendered product-audit scanner from reporting a **P0 on a page that is correct**.

## The intuition in one paragraph

`audit-app.js`'s `scanNumbers()` reads a rendered page's `innerText` and flags any bare number
whose magnitude is ≥ `ABSURD_MAGNITUDE` (1e11) — that's the detector that catches the item-122
bug class (a rate-stability score rendering −900,719,925,474,097.9). Its regex had no
**left-boundary** assertion, so it happily matched a digit run sitting *inside* an alphanumeric
token. Solana's wrapped-SOL mint address is `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`.
`PoolDetail.js` truncates EVM addresses to `0xdac1...1ec7 ↗` but renders base58 mints in full,
so that 41-digit tail lands in the page text — and the scanner read it as 1.11e+40 and cried
wolf on the north-star surface.

The fix is one assertion: a digit run preceded by a letter or digit is a fragment of a token,
not a number.

## What changed, in reading order

1. **`audit-app.js`, `scanNumbers()`** — `numRe` gains a zero-width lookbehind:

   ```diff
   -  const numRe = /(-?)\$?(\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([KMBTkmbt])?/g;
   +  const numRe = /(?<![A-Za-z0-9])(-?)\$?(\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([KMBTkmbt])?/g;
   ```

   …plus a comment above it naming spec 157 and its sibling `ABSURD_MAGNITUDE_TEXT`
   (`audit-app.js:205`), which has carried this exact predicate since 157 with the standing
   warning *"do NOT revert to the loose form."* **The predicate is identical; the form differs
   on purpose.** 157's constant is used in a single `.match()` call, so a capturing
   `(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])` alternation is harmless there. `numRe` is driven in a `/g` `exec()` loop
   that reads `n[1]`/`n[2]`/`n[3]` by fixed index and reports `n[0].trim()` verbatim — a
   capturing prefix would shift every index, splice the boundary character into the message the
   operator reads, and consume a character the next iteration may need. The lookbehind enforces
   the same condition while capturing nothing and not advancing `lastIndex`. The comment says so,
   so nobody "unifies" the two back into a bug.

2. **`test_audit_number_boundary.js`** (new, 201 lines) — 9 cases covering the spec's 7 criteria:
   5 plain (`scanNumbers` called directly, plus a guard that reads the shipped source and fails
   if the lookbehind ever disappears) and 2 real Chromium renders through `runAudit()` on ports
   8824/8825, writing to temp `outPath`s so the committed `signals/audit-findings.json` is never
   touched.

3. **`package.json`** — registers the new file in the `test:serial` chain. That chain is
   `run-tests.js`'s single source of truth for the file list (`run-tests.js:57-82`), so a test
   not listed there simply never runs.

## Why the tests are the interesting part

A boundary fix is trivially easy to ship *too wide* — narrow the match a little too much and the
detector silently stops catching the real 122 bug class, which is exactly the failure you would
not notice, because a scanner that finds nothing looks identical to a clean product.

So the acceptance is symmetric on purpose:

- **Criterion 6 (rendered, must be silent)** targets a pool that genuinely renders a raw base58
  mint — **derived from `data/pools-snapshot.json` at test time, never hardcoded**, because the
  snapshot churns daily. 28 of 741 pools qualify today; the test falls back to injecting the
  mint into a temp snapshot if that population ever hits 0.
- **Criterion 7 (rendered, must fire)** injects a real `900,719,925,474,097.9` into the same
  pool and requires the P0 back, quoting `9.01e+14`.

Silence and noise are both asserted, on a real render, on the same page.

## Deviation from the spec

One, documented in `193-notes.md`: the spec's prose wrote `poolIds: [id]`, but
`buildPoolSurfaces()` does `opts.poolIds.split(',')` — an array has no `.split`. The builder hit
the actual throw, then used the real contract (`poolIds: 'id'`, a bare string) that
`test_audit_pool_prescan.js:199` already exercises. Spec prose was wrong; the code is right.

## Residuals, documented not fixed

- **A pure-digit token ≥ 1e11 at the start of a line would still be read as a number.** Inherent:
  at that position there is no preceding character, and the text is genuinely indistinguishable
  from a magnitude. Measured population today: **0** (the only digit-leading raw token in the
  snapshot is Algorand ASA `1134696561` = 1.13e9, below the 1e11 floor).
- **`PoolDetail.js` truncates EVM addresses but renders 44-char base58 mints in full.** That
  asymmetry is *why* this false positive existed. Out of scope here — this item is about the
  scanner reporting a defect where none exists, not about changing what the page renders. Filed
  as backlog row **195**.

## Verification

Verifier verdict **PASS, 7/7** (tier LOW as assigned; re-tiered HIGH by the operator on the
line-count arithmetic in the note at the top — the PASS itself stands unchanged), independently
re-derived: it ran all six test files
itself, re-measured the 28/741 population to prove criterion 6 is not vacuous, confirmed the
rendered run really launched Chromium, and performed its own revert-and-restore cycle
(criteria 1/2/5/6 red on the loose form, 3/4/7 green; byte-identical restore confirmed against
`git show HEAD:audit-app.js`).

## Measurement

Not a growth experiment — a correctness fix to a checker, so the ≥30-event minimum-sample rule
does not apply. The metric is visible on the **very next heartbeat tick**: `number-sanity` P0
findings quoting an address fragment should go from ≥1 per tick to 0, while the tick must still
exit non-zero for a genuine P0 (criterion 7 is the standing proof of that half).

## Quiz (HIGH lane — 5 questions; answers base64 at the bottom)

1. The fix uses a zero-width lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])`, while `ABSURD_MAGNITUDE_TEXT` two
   thousand lines earlier expresses the *same* predicate as a capturing alternation
   `(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])`. Why would copying 157's form verbatim into `numRe` have been a bug rather
   than a harmless style choice?

2. Criterion 6 asserts that a rendered pool-detail page produces **zero** `number-sanity`
   findings. What would make that assertion worthless, and what specifically in the test (and in
   the verifier's independent pass) prevents it?

3. Which single acceptance criterion protects against the *opposite* failure — a fix that is too
   aggressive — and why is that failure mode harder to notice than the bug being fixed?

4. Does this change make `scanNumbers()` immune to reading address text as a number? Answer
   precisely, and give the measured number that makes the residual acceptable today.

5. `test_audit_number_boundary.js` is registered in `package.json`'s `test:serial` chain. What
   would happen if that one line were omitted, and why is it an acceptance criterion rather than
   a housekeeping detail?
